entries.postTitle: Why AI Music Tools Make Everything Sound the Same

captions.threads:
Play three AI tracks back to back and something clicks. They all breathe the same way. Same glossy pad underneath, same drum bus politeness, same emotional middle ground like someone applied a filter called "inoffensive."

I think the real issue is that these tools are trained on what already exists. They're pattern-matching machines learning from a soup of finished music. So they're architecturally incapable of the weird, the dissonant, the "wait what was that" moments that actually stick with humans.

The glitchy ones, the ones that fail in interesting ways, those are closer to something real. Not because AI is magic but because constraints breed creativity. A broken tool forces you to work around it.

If you're making music with AI and everything sounds generic, that's actually useful information. It means you gotta break the tool or use it different.

If this lands, let it change how you move today.

entries.postTitle: Rebuilding Intuition

captions.threads:
1/4 i stopped trusting my gut somewhere between age 12 and my first smartphone. not all at once, but in that slow way where you stop noticing you're doing it. every instinct got cross-checked against google, against what others said, against data i could hold in my hands. the knowing part got buried under the proving part.

2/4 what's wild is how much energy that costs. running every internal signal through external validation is like trying to drive with the parking brake on. your intuition isn't magic, it's pattern recognition operating at a speed your conscious mind can't articulate yet. but if you've trained yourself to ignore it long enough, that speed becomes invisible.

3/4 rebuilding it isn't about meditation retreats or burning sage or whatever. it's about the smallest rebellions. noticing when you feel something before you can explain it. sitting with that feeling for five seconds instead of immediately reaching for proof. testing it. letting yourself be wrong sometimes without making it mean something about your worth.

4/4 the real shift happens when you stop treating intuition and evidence like opponents. they're not. they're the same intelligence working at different frequencies. one's just faster and quieter than you've been trained to believe matters. https://vibrationofawesome.com/blog/boom/posts/rebuilding-intuition

Here's the real paradox: the people most ready for an AI mastermind are usually the ones convinced they don't need one yet.

1/3 You're already experimenting. You're already scrappy, already building weird things that don't fit traditional boxes. So adding "mastermind" to your life feels like one more obligation, one more room full of people talking about things you already half-know. But here's what shifts: it's not about learning AI. It's about learning *with* people who think like you do, who see the tools as extensions of their own weird creative nervous system instead of trend-chasing.

2/3 The in-person version matters because text-based community flattens the texture of what's actually happening. You need to sit across from someone whose music-making process is tangled up with their neurodivergence and their AI experimentation. You need to watch how another creator's hands move when they're explaining their workflow.
